    "residual": "One part of the claim is refuted: 'values derived from the secrets are masked first \u2026 never print a secret'. Suppose the DATABASE_URL password has an unencoded '@', e.g. postgresql://postgres.ref:Pa@Tail9@host/postgres. Python's urlsplit takes the password as 'Pa@Tail9', while libpq/conninfo takes 'Pa' and makes the host 'Tail9@host'. The masks registered are 'Pa', 'Pa@Tail9' and the whole URL. psycopg's error then prints \"failed to resolve host 'Tail9@host'\", which leaks the tail of the password unmasked. I reproduced this with staging.main(['migrate']) under GITHUB_ACTIONS=true. Lesser points: (a) if DATABASE_URL is set but the Supabase secrets are not, migrate still writes and only the seed reports BLOCKED. That is per-command degrade, not 'no writes when any secret is missing', which is acceptable but worth stating. (b) The staging environment has no deployment-branch rule and the workflow is dispatchable, so any branch with push access can run its own code with the staging secrets."
